findings.user_impact: The label 'Localized audio' blurs story narration and page-level audio, so an editor cannot tell which audio asset is being managed from the content detail screen.
The mockup exposes the localized reading cover and source cover but omits the shared listening cover, hiding a real story asset workflow.
The locale workspace is visually read-only: copy, duration, status, mobile visibility, processing, and publication actions are not represented as editable controls.
The header only opens the story-page mockup; it does not expose the production story preview flow with playback and page navigation.
Contributor assignments are shown as a static list, making the credits workspace look informational even though assignments, roles, language scope, and order are managed here.
Content metadata appears as three immutable values and does not represent active-state editing; this makes the shared content workspace look incomplete.
Meditation and lullaby rows in the type tables did not open a detail workspace, so type-specific editorial work was unreachable from the primary registry flow.
Using the story detail template for every type would expose story-only concepts such as pages and source illustrations where they do not apply, while hiding meditation and lullaby-specific fields.
Language-independent metadata appeared after the locale workspace, forcing editors to pass through language-specific work before reaching content-level decisions.
Tall locale tabs with repeated status labels used too much vertical space and made locale selection compete with the editing workspace.
A separate mobile-visibility action was unclear and duplicated the state-management concept represented by localization status.
Loaded image and audio cards occupied more space than necessary and did not communicate the compact selected-asset pattern used by the production asset controls.
The locale workspace repeated the current title and description in a summary card before showing the same values as editable form fields, adding noise without a separate decision or action.
The content metadata section used a technical title and repeated content type as a form field, making the shared content context feel heavier than necessary.
A separate content-details section added a large navigation stop before the locale workspace, while story preview and story-page actions were visually detached from the locale they operate on.
The page header card repeated the story title and explanatory copy already available in the locale workspace, adding vertical weight before the primary editing surface.
Meditation and lullaby detail pages used the same redundant page header pattern, leaving the back action detached from the locale workspace that owns the editing context.
